items.title: Streetsville Barbershop Owner Turns Walls Into Gallery for Local Artists and His Own Paintings
items.summary: A Streetsville barbershop called Heartbreak Hotel has become more than a place for haircuts, doubling as a showcase for local art and streetwear. According to the Toronto Star, owner Omar Preza, 44, was born in El Salvador and raised in Canada, and built the shop around his lifelong passions for drawing, comic books and street graffiti. The newspaper reported that customers walk in to upbeat Latin and hip-hop music, with painted canvases in thrifted gold frames and custom apparel hanging from industrial pipe racks against black-and-white brick walls. The Star said Heartbreak Hotel began in 2013 as a streetwear clothing brand, with Preza starting to paint around the same time, and today he sells both his original fine art and custom-designed apparel in the shop alongside the haircuts. His work was included in the Art Gallery of Mississauga's 2024-2025 Fourth Annual Juried Show of Visual Arts, according to the paper.

items.title: Budget-Priced Danish Retailer Set to Open Square One Location Next Week
items.summary: A Danish variety chain known for quirky, low-cost home goods is set to open its first Mississauga location at Square One Shopping Centre on Saturday, Nov. 14. According to insauga.com, Flying Tiger Copenhagen will open a sister store at CF Markville in Markham two days earlier, on Nov. 12. The outlet reported the retailer stocks home decor, stationery, toys, kitchenware, party supplies and seasonal items, with more than 80 per cent of its products priced under $10. Roughly 300 new items arrive in its stores each month, insauga.com said. The chain traces its roots to Copenhagen in 1995, when it launched under the name Tiger, and now runs more than 1,000 stores across 45 markets, with Canada becoming its 45th this year. Its first Canadian store opened at CF Toronto Eaton Centre in June, and the company has said the GTA marks its first step into a wider rollout across the Americas. CEO Jens Aarup Mikkelsen said in a release that the company sees strong alignment with Canadian shoppers who want design-led products at accessible prices. Stores are laid out like a maze so customers pass through all 14 product categories, according to insauga.com.

items.title: Dixie Road Tops List as Nearly 300 Vehicles Stolen Across Mississauga and Brampton in a Month
items.summary: Peel Regional Police data shows thieves stole 283 vehicles across Mississauga and Brampton between Oct. 7 and Nov. 7, averaging about nine thefts a day. According to insauga.com, Mississauga accounted for 167 of those thefts while Brampton saw 116. The outlet reported that cars made up the bulk of the stolen vehicles, with 201 automobiles taken alongside 60 trucks, 17 motorcycles and five vehicles in other categories. In Mississauga, Dixie Road saw the most thefts with 10 reported, followed by nine on Airport Road, five on Argentia Road, four on Britannia Road and three in the City Centre area. Brampton's hot spots included seven thefts on Great Lakes Drive and four each on Bramtree Court and Coventry Road, insauga.com said. Peel police are asking anyone with information to call 905-453-3311 or contact Peel Crime Stoppers anonymously at 1-800-222-TIPS.

items.title: Legal Experts Say Law Is Unclear on Filming Police During Live Operations
items.summary: A tense standoff with an armed suspect at the University of Toronto's Mississauga campus has sparked a debate over whether it's appropriate to livestream police movements during an active incident. According to CBC Toronto, officers responding to the Monday night standoff issued a stern warning after social media users posted real-time footage showing police positions on the scene. The broadcaster reported that legal experts say Canadian law offers no clear-cut answer on whether filming and sharing an active police operation crosses a line, since it sits at the intersection of free expression and officer safety. CBC Toronto said police have long worried that revealing tactical positions in real time could tip off a suspect and put officers and bystanders at risk. The debate echoes similar controversies in other cities, where livestreamed footage of active incidents has drawn scrutiny from both civil liberties advocates and law enforcement. CBC Toronto noted the broader legal question remains unresolved.

items.title: Mississauga's Laeticia Amihere Becomes Second Canadian Ever to Win a WNBA Title
items.summary: Laeticia Amihere, a 25-year-old forward from Mississauga, became just the second Canadian ever to win a WNBA championship after her Golden State Valkyries beat the Atlanta Dream 68-63 in Game 7 of the Finals. According to the Toronto Star, Amihere was introduced as the team's enforcer at a victory parade Wednesday that drew an estimated 400,000 fans to the San Francisco Bay Area, and told the paper the nickname fits since she has always been known for her tenacity. The Star reported Amihere previously won gold with Canada's under-16 team at the 2015 FIBA Americas championship, took third at the 2017 under-19 World Cup and won an NCAA title with the South Carolina Gamecocks in 2022. She did not see the court in Game 7 but had 10 rebounds in 20 minutes in Game 6, contributing to a Valkyries team that won it all in just its second season. The only other Canadian to win a WNBA championship is Markham's Tammy Sutton-Brown, who did so with the Indiana Fever in 2012, the paper said. Amihere is set to travel to Senegal next week to continue work with her sports non-profit, Back to the Motherland.

items.title: Residents' Groups Push for a Voice in City Hall Spending as Tedjo Faces His First Budget
items.summary: Frustrated by what they see as limited influence over City Hall's budget decisions, a Mississauga residents' association is pushing for a bigger voice as the city prepares its 2027 budget. According to The Pointer, Athina Tagidou, president of the Applewood Heights Residents' Association, said she believes resident input into municipal spending is minimal despite her group's efforts attending budget meetings, organizing consultations and pressing for independent financial oversight. The outlet reported that incoming mayor Alvin Tedjo, who has served on council for four years, will now prepare his first budget as residents' associations and taxpayers watch closely. Tedjo campaigned on freezing Mississauga's share of the property tax for two years while finding efficiencies within the municipal corporation, The Pointer said. Tagidou and other residents are questioning where those savings will come from and whether the city can maintain existing services and infrastructure without the cuts catching up with taxpayers later, according to the outlet. The Pointer noted the 2027 budget will serve as an early test of whether Tedjo can deliver on the promises that helped him unseat two veteran mayoral candidates.

items.title: Mississauga's Goat-Grazing Program to Continue Through 2027 After Early Success
items.summary: The City of Mississauga plans to keep using herds of grazing goats to fight invasive plant species through 2027 and beyond, after three years of what officials call a groundbreaking success. According to insauga.com, the city has brought in the goats each spring through early fall since 2024, using the animals as natural lawnmowers to control non-native species like buckthorn, phragmites and reed canary grass in meadows and prairies. Mississauga was the first municipality in Ontario to use goat grazing for invasive species control when it launched the program, the outlet reported. City spokesperson Irene McCutcheon told insauga.com the grazing has reduced the extent, density and size of invasive plant populations at treated sites, with the strongest results coming at sites that have been grazed repeatedly. McCutcheon said those sites have generally needed little to no follow-up manual control. Beyond the environmental results, she said the goats have also become ambassadors for the city's invasive species and pest management program through events like the annual Invasive Species Awareness Fair.
